evidence_anchor.anchor: text: §2.4 "with poorly contacting electrodes, unspecified in advance, for cardiac-output estimation from thoracic EIT data (Murphy et al., 2019)"
text: letter REV-R3-10 "R2-W4 not accepted. The PubMed abstract states that the network was trained on EIT data for cardiac-output estimation, so the citation stays as an EIT example"

adjustments.rationale: The round-2 finding R2-W4 rested on the paper's title ('by its own title, a bioimpedance approach ... to my knowledge it is not an EIT ... study; I also cannot confirm from memory that the degradation it drew was unspecified poor electrode contact'), and the committed sub-check (3) inherited that premise ('Murphy et al. (bioimpedance cardiac-output)'). The letter's rebuttal was not taken on its say-so: this seat retrieved the PubMed record on 2026-10-07 (PMID 30840932, doi 10.1088/1361-6579/ab0d45). Its abstract reads 'Machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on electrical-impedance tomography (EIT) data are presented for portable cardiac monitoring. The approach was validated on a simulated thorax and a measured tank experiment ... The ML algorithms were trained using databases that assumed the presence of poorly contacting electrodes without any assumptions of knowing which electrodes would be bad in the experiment.' That supports both halves of the v4 clause (thoracic EIT data; poorly contacting electrodes, unspecified in advance), matches the wording 35_CITATION_AUDIT_v4.md records, and shows that filing Murphy 2019 as an EIT precedent is correct, so the premise of the original finding is false and the rebuttal is valid on the merits. Sub-checks (1) Graf, (2) GREIT/Pulletz with the matching Fig. 2 legend, and (4) Frerichs 2002 as entry 12 under the DIS-1 corrected descriptor (IEEE Trans Med Imaging 21:646–652) were already verified by 2A; the 54-entry list is present. No residual.

new_issues.description: The new §3.2 paragraph closes with 'the capacity control removes 0.12 points of it at most', but the direction is reversed: Table S9 gives B_wide − B ≤ 0 at every level (−0.037 to −0.124), so the capacity-controlled contrast D − B_wide exceeds the uncontrolled D − B at every level, by 0.124 points at 20 dB (2.097 against 1.973). Replacing B with the widened control adds up to 0.12 points to the advantage; it removes none. The paragraph's conclusion that width does not explain the advantage still holds, but an adversarial reader will note that the control is conservative in the opposite direction from the one stated.
